record.rationale: Browser and DOM-free Worker host events implement the actual native SalTimer plugin boundary while queue ownership,priority selection and task lifecycle remain with the separate upstream VCL scheduler.
responsibilities: Actual browser/Worker single-shot host timer implements SalTimer,using current callback dispatch,pending-event replacement,cancellation and explicit destruction. The old handle is released before callback entry so native reentrant restart survives. Unsigned64 arguments are converted at the boundary;delays above signed32 host capacity are capped for the native scheduler deadline recheck,avoiding JavaScript overflow-to-immediate. Upstream QtTimer is also single-shot;browser event scheduling replaces the native Sal plugin. Full native scheduler/OS input/threads are not represented by this platform adapter.

stackDivergence.rationale: JavaScript host timers replace Qt/X11/macOS/Windows event-loop timers;native VCL task scheduling remains above this boundary.
